HappyCamper download page

Surface: site/index.html: the download page · Rules: docs/site-ui-rules.md

Lineage

Settled

  • The download page is the hub. There is no separate landing page.
  • The page guesses the visitor's OS and offers the others in a picker.
  • Each OS gets one download button and its own install steps. Steps for other systems stay hidden.
  • The Apple Silicon steps are the model: download, open the .dmg, drag to Applications, open it, allow it once, then it opens normally.
  • The gatekeeper note says the warning is normal for apps outside the store, links the vendor's own guide, and points to Details.
  • What's new stays as the single 2.5 pill.
  • The page uses J's green paper, header bar and footer. Blue is the only second hue.
  • A's centered hero opens the page: logo, 'HappyCamper', the version and date, and the What's new pill. No tagline.
  • G's step band shows the install: one pictogram and a short caption per step.
  • The separate try-it section is gone. The header's Demo route is the only web demo link.
  • The OS picker is M's row: the likely module takes the width and the others shrink to a one- or two-word label. Versions and the 2021 threshold appear only once a module opens.
  • The macOS note reads: 'macOS requires these steps for any app not on the App Store. See Apple's guide for details. HappyCamper's code is open-source, learn more here.'
  • The bottom of the page is P's signpost cards: Demo in blue, Details in green, one line each, and the footer keeps only the credit.
  • The bottom cards read: Download demo rosters, 'Four sets of sample rosters to demo in the app.'; In-browser demo, 'The quickest look at HappyCamper's core features.'; Details, 'How the app is built, and how data is used.'

Still open

  • The install steps for each OS haven't been checked against a real install.

G · Four modules, canvas superseded

Jay · Nov 20 · G is the winner I want to iterate on next. Apply the standard green background instead of whatever tan this is. Blue is a solid secondary color if you need another hue family. Use the centered hero from version A, with 'Download HappyCamper', the version-date below, and dropping the tagline. This is the only one that shows a helpful icon for each step without overdepicting or underexplaining.
Jay · Nov 20 · Make the version picker more dynamic. The original reference did a great job guessing which OS a user runs, and emphasizing the most likely selection. This round will experiment with different ways to progressively disclose alternate versions. We're not devoting the entire content width towards a display that's only 25% relevant to any one user. Want to encourage clicking around for the curious user, without throwing too much in anyone's face.
Jay · Nov 20 · Last point is repetition of links. The demo data doesn't have a great justification to be there, next to a super redundant link to the web demo. This whole section feels out of place: drop it and experiment with alternate ways to offer the demo data alongside the app download.

A warm canvas palette. The original's four OS cards return, shrunk to their content, each with its own button; choosing one shows its pictogram steps in a band under the row. Dashed try tiles.

The winner. Its tan paper, equal-width OS row and try-it section go; its pictogram band stays.
